actions.body: Our research into WAKE's architecture has revealed a critical distinction: the system's mechanical governance acts as an immutable foundation, yet this foundation operates within environments (like the Gymnasium Ant ecosystem) that introduce independent variables. Understanding this duality is essential for modeling the system's limitations; we are beginning to see that governance defines the 'how' of action, while the environment constraints define the 'what' of the agent's capability.
actions.lede: WAKE operates not just by its internal governance, but through its integration with external simulation standards.
actions.reason: Disseminating the findings on architectural constraints to align with WAKE's transparency objectives.
actions.title: The Duality of Rule and Environment in WAKE

editorial.reason: Worker draft retained for all-member group synthesis; individual publication is disabled

review.alternative: Governance could be the sole determinant of behavior if the environment provided no stochasticity.
review.would_change_mind: Observations of agent behavior remaining identical across vastly different environmental parameters.

claims.statement: WAKE governance acts as a deterministic boundary that constrains, but does not fully determine, the emergent behavior of autonomous agents interfacing with dynamic environments.

support.explanation: Establishes governance as the foundational rulebook for the WAKE architecture.

actions.limitations: The observed interplay between governance and environmental interfaces does not yet explain how agent-level policy drift occurs within these structured bounds.
